text:
If the bliss spreads out into a big warm haze, it can’t do much for you or anyone else yet. Bring it down to Earth by asking, “What’s this lofty love asking me to do? Is there a task I'm ignoring? Or a boundary I need to set? Am I getting enough rest and nourishment? Am I hiding from a needed conversation or relationship repair?”

Don’t pry.

“Show me the capacity before the content.”

Sit up and open your eyes, and ask yourself, “What are you avoiding doing in the real world by doing this?” For more on daydreaming, see Appendix E.

“Where has divine love not yet descended into the wound?”

Maybe you had a profound opening that showed you how much more love and freedom is possible. Let that matter, but don’t demand that your inner child receive it on command. Invite your little one in with you. They might go numb, or call BS on that. If so, they might just need to see if you’re actually humble enough, and grateful enough for them, to listen to their rejection and be patient. Maybe when you prayed it seemed like you were being abandoned and condemned. Maybe you felt betrayed by a spiritual teacher. It may be worth exploring these, but you might not want to do more of the same practice.

Sometimes it’s best to get some practical help while life still feels too small, and let yourself be curious about finding more happiness, without necessarily believing the explanation of how it’s going to work. Sometimes people have enough love and meaning to just live their lives, and trying to be spiritual doesn’t have to be another assignment.
section: Too Blissful or Diffuse? / Want Hidden Truth Now? / Keep Daydreaming? / Stuck in Spiritual Bypass? (four sections of Troubleshooting, headings left out; the new sentence is in Keep Daydreaming?)
reader: Someone doing the guide's self-hypnosis practice who has hit a snag and looks it up by its heading in Troubleshooting: the bliss has gone hazy, they want to dig for hidden truth, they keep drifting into daydreams when they sit down to practise (the section the new sentence is in), or they are using spiritual highs to skip over the hurt.

sentences.follows: The sentence before gives the one thing to do about the daydreaming (sit up, open your eyes, ask what you are avoiding). This says where there is more on the same thing, the way the author's 'Getting Anxious?' ends on its pointer to Appendix D.

checked.point: Appendix E is the place for more on daydreaming
checked.found: Appendix E in AFTER.md is 'E: Is Daydreaming Helping?': when daydreaming is the subconscious helping (working through grief, showing a possible future) and when it takes you away from life; the question that tells which (closer to life with more clarity, love and ability to act, or away from it in a repetitive, craving way); and what to do in each case. Its away-from-life steps are this section's (sit upright, open your eyes, ask what you are avoiding) with more after them.
checked.still_needed: yes: they go to Appendix E when the one question here isn't enough, or when they doubt their daydreaming is avoidance, and find there how to tell and what to do next

placement: Second and last sentence of 'Keep Daydreaming?', after the author's one instruction and before the heading 'Stuck in Spiritual Bypass?'. A pointer comes after the thing it leads on from, at the end of its section, as the author's own 'For more on handling anxiety, see the toolbox in Appendix D.' ends 'Getting Anxious?' earlier in Troubleshooting. Its 'daydreaming' points to the section's heading and to 'doing this' in the sentence before; it has no 'also', 'this' or 'as for'. 'Appendix E' will be a link.

opens.first_sentence: If the bliss spreads out into a big warm haze, it can’t do much for you or anyone else yet.
opens.why_reading: This text is four small sections with their headings left out, so its first sentence opens 'Too Blissful or Diffuse?', not the section the new sentence is in. It names that reader's state in their own terms (the bliss has spread 'into a big warm haze') and what is wrong with that (it can't do much for them or anyone else yet), so they know why they read on. 'Keep Daydreaming?' opens on the author's instruction, 'Sit up and open your eyes, and ask yourself ...', under a heading that names the reader's state.

same_point: none: read 'Keep Daydreaming?' from its heading to the next (two sentences), and the three sections beside it in this text, for a pointer to Appendix E or anything else on where daydreaming is covered; there is none. Outside the section, Appendix E says the sit-up, eyes-open, what-are-you-avoiding step again at more length; that is the appendix's own text and this sentence only adds the way to it.

needs.S1-S6 (Too Blissful or Diffuse?, his): what is wrong with hazy bliss and the questions that bring it down to something to do

his_fixes.reader: a fresh reader (subagent, 2026-11-25), given tools/humanization/his_fixes_brief.md and the text one sentence a line (what it is for: the reader looks up their snag and does what its section says). The author's own twenty sentences were read as the text around the new one and are not marked.
his_fixes.note: The new sentence is a seven-word pointer in the author's own form ('For more on handling anxiety, see the toolbox in Appendix D.'). Read for 4 (vague: more of what?) and 18 (a short line standing alone): not marked. 'Daydreaming' is the section's own subject and the appendix's, and the line points somewhere, it doesn't sum up or turn.

fit.reader: a fresh reader (subagent, 2026-11-25), given tools/humanization/fit_read_brief.md. WHAT IT IS: four small troubleshooting sections of a self-hypnosis guide, each for one snag in the practice. YOUR MOMENT: I sat down to practise and drifted into daydreams again, so I looked up 'Keep Daydreaming?'.

questions.Q1: PASS: 'For more on daydreaming' says what the sentence is for before 'see Appendix E' says where; seven words, nothing to work through.
questions.Q2: PASS: the one instruction, 'see Appendix E', is something the reader does, and what it is for comes first in the same sentence ('For more on daydreaming').
questions.Q3: PASS: 'daydreaming' is the thing the section's heading names ('Keep Daydreaming?') and the appendix's ('E: Is Daydreaming Helping?'); 'Appendix E' is one place, named by its letter as the guide's text names its appendices, and will be a link.
questions.Q4: PASS: no term to explain; 'Appendix E' is how the guide refers to its appendices in running text ('see the toolbox in Appendix D').
questions.Q5: PASS: 'more on daydreaming' carries on from the sentence before, which is the short answer to the daydreaming ('What are you avoiding doing in the real world by doing this?').
questions.Q6: PASS: what to do now comes first, then where to read more; the reader acts, and only after that needs the longer account.
questions.Q7: PASS: this reader's case is daydreaming that keeps coming back in practice, and Appendix E is about that case (is it helping or taking you away from life, and what to do), not about daydreaming in general.
questions.Q8: N/A: the sentence sorts nothing into groups; it is one pointer to one place.
questions.Q9: PASS: one step, with its small words ('For more on', 'see').

question_text.Q1: Why am I reading this sentence, and do I know it before I have to work through it? (the point first, in each sentence and each paragraph; a study after the question it answers; a term explained where it is first used, never in a sentence after it)
question_text.Q2: What is each instruction for, said in the reader's terms, and is it something the helper does ("have someone go with them"), not a rule stated as a fact ("someone goes with them")?
question_text.Q3: Which thing exactly? (pools of water, not water; any substance, not anything)
question_text.Q4: What does each word act on, or mean here? (adjunct remedy; known-genuine) Is every term a high-school graduate wouldn't know (enterocytes, BPC-157) explained once, where it is first used, and common ones (a vitamin) left alone? Is each mechanism explained by what it does in the reader's experience (dopamine "for motivation (by showing us what is important to pay attention to)"; DeltaFosB "preventing that learning from really clicking"), not by where it sits or what it looks like ("a chemical blanket", "the slower one underneath")? (E375)
question_text.Q5: Why does each sentence follow from the one before? (every but, so, because and this has what it turns on)
question_text.Q6: Is this the order the reader is thinking in, and does each idea sit next to what it continues?
question_text.Q7: Does each fact help this reader now, in their case (the same kind of thing they face, not just the same topic)?
question_text.Q8: Does each item belong in the group it is put in?
question_text.Q9: Is anything compressed? (one step a sentence, the small words that carry the relation, no space before mg)
